t: This Act shall take effect ninety days after the date of its enactment.

fable.w: This is a bare effective-date clause that sets when the Act takes effect. It involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision. There is no tempting contrary reading, since nothing in the text is procedural.
fable.s: This Act shall take effect ninety days after the date of its enactment.

qwen_block.s: This Act shall take effect ninety days after the date of its enactment.

opus.w: This section only sets the date the Act takes effect, ninety days after enactment. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking authority, or right to sue. Nothing in it touches outside participation, so no span is quoted.
opus.b: I'm labelling this **No**. There's no tempting reading to rule out. The section is only an effective-date clause. It sets when the Act starts to apply, and no one outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely establishes the effective date of the Act. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government. The delay is automatic and does not involve any procedural interaction with the public, states, or other external entities.
qwen_chat.s: This Act shall take effect ninety days after the date of its enactment.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the 90-day delay allows for public comment or consultation before the law takes effect. However, the text itself does not mandate any such process; it simply sets a start date. There is no mention of hearings, comments, or advisory bodies.
